description: Golden reference for calc_accel_magnet.py on the C-type dipole em_1-1_full.jou (1/1 full geometry, linear mu_r=1000).
rationale: Regression guard for the no-reduction baseline.  The yoke spans its full extent in all three axes (x, y, z); the air is a complete sphere with a z=0 mesh seam (geometry full, seam for Kelvin copy-mesh only).  Auto-Kelvin detects symmetry=['z'] from the air's volume centroids straddling z=0 (NOT from vertex range -- that older heuristic spuriously triggered 'x' too on a multi-vol z-only-webcut sphere).  The Kelvin sphere is offset along +x by 3R, webcut at z=0 to match the air's hemispheres.  No sym sidesets, no kelvin_far -- just kelvin_int / kelvin_ext periodic + GND.

sample.generator_cmd_note: Regenerate via Cubit batch: play em_1-1_full.jou + play auto_kelvin_entry.py (with kelvin_reduction=null) + export netgen order=2 overwrite.

geometry_note: Full geometry baseline: yoke at x in [-12.5, +12.5], y in [0, 182.5], z in [-26.25, +26.25] mm; air sphere radius 0.40 m centred at origin, with z=0 mesh seam (both hemispheres retained).  Kelvin sphere is full + offset along +x.  This is the largest of the 4 variants (8x more DOFs than 1/8).

observations.note: Absolute-value snapshot for regression guard.  Reference baseline -- reductions (1/2, 1/4, 1/8) impose sym BCs that change the field; the FULL model is the cleanest physics-realistic case for the C-yoke geometry.  Run time ~19 min on LAB (PARDISO factorization of 75k DOFs SPD matrix).
